mission.title: The Internuncio
mission.description: Protect an important Matrix artifact for Zion.

npc.say: Have you spoken to Gagarin yet?
Maybe we'll get to work together in the future.
Maybe we'll get to work together in the future.

phase.briefing:
We've experienced some backlash from a separate assignment -- a group of Exiles recently attacked one of our bases. Our operative, Campbell, was there when the strike took place. She is lucky to be alive!
Meet with Campbell and get the statue from her. We need this statue transported to a safer location. Once you've left the area with the statue, I will update you with the drop-off point.

talk.say: Good, you're here. Tyndall told me to expect you. It isn't exactly safe here anymore, so we need this statue moved to a new location.
Take the statue from Campbell by right-clicking the mouse and selecting the "Get" interaction.

done.say:
I'm glad Campbell was able to hold off the Exiles until you arrived.
Campbell will be fine. Just worry about the statue. Once you've exited the area I will send you the drop-off location.
See to it that Gagarin gets this. The statue is a Matrix artifact that has been around for many years now. We cannot allow this to fall into enemy hands!

near.say: Campbell is waiting for you. Identify yourself and get the statue from her.

phase.briefing: You're doing well, {player}. I'm sending you Gagarin's coordinates now. Deliver the statue to her.

talk.say:
Those Exiles won't let up, will they? They insist on making trouble for us within the Matrix.
Well, enough of that... Do you have the statue with you?
That's her. You may give her the statue. To do this, right-click on her and select the "Give" interaction.

done.say: You're done here, {player}. Leave the area and Tyndall will debrief you.
Thank you, {player}. I'll secure the statue.

near.say: Gagarin is stationed at the Zion base inside this building. She'll take the statue from you.

mission.finish: You have Zion's thanks, Warrior. Contact me when you are ready for your next assignment.
